title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + rope/rotary fused ops + KV continuous batching
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Upgrade the serving runtime attention implementation to the newer FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fold fused rotary/ROPE operations and KV projection ops into the attention path. This patch also enables continuous KV batching across micro-batches to reduce kernel invocation overhead for medium-length sequences. The combined change targets production tails (latency-sensitive 2-8 token generations) and throughput-heavy batching workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Wire in vendor/third_party flashattn_v2 kernels and expose a runtime selection flag (ATTN_KERNEL=flashattnv2).
- Implement fused rotary/ROPE application inside the attention kernel to avoid separate elementwise kernels for rotary multiplication.
- Fuse KV projection (Q/K/V linear) with packing into the kernel when quantization/precision profile allows.
- Add continuous KV batching scheduler in the runtime: carryover KV queues between micro-batches and perform larger attention kernel calls when latency/SLO permits.
- Add a gated rollout flag (runtime.config.enable_fused_attn=true) and a model-capability check to only enable for known compatible transformer variants.

Performance summary (detailed results in CI/benchmarks):
- p50 latency improvement on chat_small workload: -12%
- throughput increase (tokens/sec) on gpt-medium batch=16: +18%
- GPU memory working-set reduction: -7% on typical 8k context runs
- End-to-end cost estimate: ~10-14% lower token cost for mixed latency/throughput workloads

Compatibility and safety: 
- Fallback path preserved. If kernel fails or model not whitelisted, runtime falls back to previous stable attention implementation (flashattn_v1 / separate rotary).
- Added a comprehensive numeric validation harness comparing 32-bit and quantized paths to the baseline for ~50 representative prompts. RMS/MAE deltas are within acceptable thresholds defined in ENG-3124.

Testing and CI: 
- Unit tests for fused rotary and fused KV packing added under runtime/tests/attn_fused_test.cc.
- End-to-end smoke and perf harness runs in perf-canary produced stable improvements; one flaky test was fixed in this PR (see review thread).
- CI status: all Linux GPU builds + integration tests passed; macOS lint and docs checks passed.

Rollout plan: 
1) Deploy behind runtime.config.enable_fused_attn gating and feature flag per-customer.
2) Canary on dedicated pools with capacity isolation for 48 hours.
3) Gradual ramp to hosted API with traffic-based auto-disable on any regression alarms.

Checklist:
- [x] Numeric validation and unit tests
- [x] Perf regression and micro-benchmark runs recorded
- [x] Feature gated and model whitelisting implemented
- [x] Documentation updates for runtime flags and troubleshooting

Notes: This PR bundles multiple close changes to minimize transitional code paths. If reviewers prefer, I can split gating/flag scaffolding into a separate PR, but the combined change is easier to benchmark end-to-end.

review_comments: Diego: Great performance wins. Please add more detail on numeric error bounds for quantized fused path.
Aisha: Added numeric validation harness and summary in tests; expanded ENG-3124 reference in description.
Hannah: Can we ensure the carried-over KV queue doesn't increase tail latency for single-request workloads? Consider a budgeted carryover window.
Aisha: Implemented budgeted carryover with configurable window and a hard latency SLO bail-out (runtime.config.kv_carry_window_ms).
Samir: CI flake observed in attn_fused_test on macOS runner; looks like RNG seed sensitivity. Recommend deterministic seed in harness.
Aisha: Fixed test seed and added deterministic sample set. Re-ran CI and green.

release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/ROPE and fused KV packing; enabled continuous KV batching. Expected improvements: ~10-18% throughput, lower p50 latency, and reduced GPU working set. Rollout gated behind runtime.feature flags.
